title: FDE Flow Pattern
description: A reusable flow shape extracted from real deployments. A pattern ships the stable 80% — the shape, the design commitments, the staffing roles, and the interview checklist for discovering the client-specific 20% — and deliberately never ships finished code. The 20% is the engagement.

pattern_version.description: Version of the flow-pattern spec this document conforms to.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier. Manifests reference this from flows[].pattern.

problem.description: The business pain this shape addresses, in the words a client would use to describe it. Not an architecture summary.

signals.description: Observable symptoms that this pattern applies — things you would actually see or hear at the client. Most should be true before reaching for the pattern.

not_for.description: Situations where this pattern looks right and is wrong. The most valuable list in the file: patterns fail by being applied, not by being unknown.

base_shape.description: The stable 80%: the path, what the flow must own, and the design rules that are not up for negotiation.

trigger_kinds.description: Trigger kinds this shape supports, using the manifest's trigger vocabulary.

steps.description: The canonical path, at the altitude a manifest flow's steps are written at. These become the starting steps of an instantiated flow.

state.description: What the flow must track in a store it owns, and why that store is not the client's system of record.

commitments.description: Design rules that hold across every instantiation. Violating one is not customization, it is a different pattern.

variation_points.description: The named knobs — decisions every instantiation must make. Each choice made at a client should be recorded as a manifest decision with the rejected options.

when.description: The client condition under which this option is right.

consequence.description: What choosing it costs or commits you to.

default.description: The option to take absent evidence. Must be one of the listed choices; the validator checks.

default_because.description: Why this is the default, ideally traceable to a real deployment's recorded decision or debt.

glue_checklist.description: The interview for discovering the client-specific 20%. Every answer has a home in the manifest — the checklist and the manifest are two views of the same discipline.

why_it_matters.description: The failure that happens when this goes unasked.

recorded_in.description: The manifest path where the answer belongs.

human_roles.description: The staffing surface. Roles are the stable unit — people rotate through them as tenures in a manifest flow's lineage. Each role's walkthrough outline is the template for the client-specific walkthrough asset.

role.description: Kebab-case role name, matching the role field of lineage tenures in manifests that instantiate this pattern.

cadence.description: How often and how long. This is what makes the role staffable.

transition_walkthrough_must_cover.description: What a handover into this role must transfer. Instantiate as a walkthrough in the client manifest and reference it from the incoming tenure's trained_via.

failure_design.description: The failures this shape is known to meet, each paired with the design response. These are pre-answered so instantiations do not rediscover them in production.

manifest_bindings.description: What instantiating this pattern obligates you to create in the client's deployment manifest.

systems.description: Which system entries must exist, described generically.

entities.description: Which entity entries must exist, including what their identifier caveats must cover.

decisions_expected.description: Decisions every instantiation will inevitably make. Naming them here is what gets them recorded instead of merely made.

tension.description: The trade-off being resolved — what pulls in each direction.

constraints_expected.description: Constraint entries an instantiation should expect to record.

metrics.description: What to baseline before building and measure after. These feed the engagement's outcomes section.

instantiations.description: The pattern's own family tree: every deployment it was extracted from or applied to, with how each deviated. Deviations are data — three instantiations deviating the same way means the pattern is wrong, not the clients.

manifest.description: Path or URL of the deployment manifest.

maturity.description: Honest provenance. A pattern with no deployments behind it is a sketch, and must say so.

status.description: extracted: distilled from at least one shipped deployment. provisional: designed, not yet proven — every default is a hypothesis.

evidence.description: What the status rests on: which deployments, and which parts remain unproven.
